newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Avoid Mexico's Serfin.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Avoid Mexico's Serfin.

text.p: Latin American brokers LatInvest on Thursday rated Mexican financial group Serfin "unattractive" and recommended investors avoid investing in the company for the time being.

"We recommend that investors avoid investing in Grupo Financiero Serfin until clear signs of operating improvement are evident," LatInvest analyst Gustavo Teran said in a research note released in London.

"Given the false starts of the past two years, we would want to see at least a couple of quarters of across-the-board sustainable improvements in net interest margin, fee income, substantial expense reduction, and progress towards finding a strategic partner."
Serfin disappointed investors on Tuesday when it turned in a third quarter loss of 507 million pesos, due mostly to 700 million pesos in bad loan provisions at its Banca Serfin unit.
LatInvest said structural problems at Banca Serfin meant it was a long way from being able to generate the operating profits necessary to cover those provisions.

Its net interest margin in the quarter contracted by 100 basis points to a low of 2.8 percent, compared with second quarter margins at rival banks Bancomer GFBB.MX, with 8.4 percent, and Banamex BAVB.MX, with 6.7 percent.
It did not see an adequate improvement in the net interest margin appearing before 1999, and this would not get any easier as the competitive environment toughens.
Credit quality remains a major concern, with classified C, D and E loans growing by 41 percent.

After a recent rights offering and a $290 million capital infusion via a JP Morgan loan, the bank was very likely to need recapitalisation due to its inability to create loan loss provisions from operating income.

"Although the stock price is at only 0.8 times book value, the potential for further dilution is high and book value will decline due to the losses induced by high loan loss provisions," Teran said, adding LatInvest rated the stock "unattractive". --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734; fax 583 7239
